newsitem.title: USA: Sierra to sell exit modem chip business.
newsitem.headline: Sierra to sell exit modem chip business.

text.p: Sierra Semiconductor Corp. said Wednesday it will stop making computer chips for modems, sell its product line and take a $50 million to $80 million charge in the third quarter.

The San Jose, Calif.-based company said stiff competition is pressuring prices and margins, while inventories in distribution channels are increasing and supply is building. It said it sees no signs that those trends will reverse.
Sierra Semiconductor, a maker of semiconductor chips, said it will now focus on manufacturing products for the growing computer infrastructure and networking markets.
Due to the change in business focus, president and chief operating officer Richard Koeltl will leave the company. Diller will assume his duties.
The company said the exact size of the charge will be determined throughout the quarter ending Sept. 30, and will be announced along with its third-quarter earnings report in October.
Sierra's stock fell 25 cents to close at $9.25 on Nasdaq.
